name: Illegalism
summary: Illegalism is a current of individualist anarchism, mainly French and Italian around 1880-1914, that treated crime as a form of revolt. Its adherents held that theft (individual reclamation), burglary, forgery and violence against the bourgeoisie were legitimate ways to live free of wage labor and to provoke revolution at once. They rejected the state, law, property and conventional morality, and were criticised by other anarchists as selfish and ineffective.
scope: The French and Italian illegalists of roughly 1880-1914: Clement Duval, Marius Jacob and his Travailleurs de la Nuit, Vittorio Pini, Ravachol and the Bonnot Gang. Based on Jacob's 1905 trial statement and secondary accounts. Excludes later anarchists who merely tolerated expropriation, and Jacob's 1948 doubts about illegalism.

keyFigures.name: Clement Duval
keyFigures.role: Often considered the founder of illegalism; defended individual reclamation at his 1887 trial.

keyFigures.name: Marius Jacob
keyFigures.role: Led the burglary band the Workers of the Night and gave the best-known statement of illegalist principles.

public-ownership.rationale: Hostile to the state in principle, and reclamation aimed at individuals' gain, not at handing industries to a state.

unions-good.rationale: Illegalists criticised the focus on the working class and trade unions as a path to change.

property-fundamental.rationale: Jacob called individual property the most unjust of thefts and rejected morality that treats respect for it as a virtue.

cut-welfare.rationale: Never addressed; they scorned state palliatives but not on dependency grounds.

worker-ownership.rationale: Individualist reclaimers rather than collectivists, yet Jacob wanted wealth shared; adherents split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: They rejected the authority of courts and laws to judge anyone, and speech laws were used against anarchists.

strong-leader.rationale: Anarchist rejection of rulers and obedience; Duval refused deference even to a police commissioner.

state-harmful.rationale: Jacob denied any right of courts to judge him and condemned the laws and institutions as serving the rich.

limit-guns.rationale: Jacob's band went armed and used weapons in self-defense; disarmament by law cuts against that.

rehabilitation.rationale: Jacob said repression only aggravates the evil, and prisons and penal colonies were brutal.

traditional-family.rationale: Hégot's 1903 letter rejected the Fatherland, Society and Morality, and illegalists scorned bourgeois morals.

more-religion-public.rationale: Jacob's band robbed priests and left graffiti mocking god; Jacob mocked promises of paradise.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Hégot rejected the Fatherland and its morality as constraints on the individual.

gradual-change.rationale: Illegalists wanted to provoke revolt immediately and had grown tired of waiting.

revolution-justified.rationale: Illegalists saw their acts as revolution itself, and Jacob said "I made my revolution".

central-planning.rationale: State direction contradicts their individualist, anti-state stance.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Anti-state; Duval did not want property merely to change hands to another owner.

widespread-small-property.rationale: They rejected individual property, though a diffuse-property picture is not directly addressed.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Jacob objected to wage work as exploitation and foresaw wealth belonging to everyone, though they lived by taking money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies are the opposite of illegalist outlawry.

one-party-rule.rationale: Wikipedia notes anarchists opposed the state itself as the institution legitimising domination, and illegalists rejected waiting on organised mass movements, so a ruling party has no place.

democracy-best.rationale: Jacob scorned "your institutions" and denied anyone's right to judge him, rejecting parliamentary order.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inference from their individualist anti-state outlook (s1): withdrawing from any authority is welcome, but regional secession from a country is not something the sources discuss.

political-violence-never.rationale: They practised propaganda of the deed, bombings and armed robbery.

separate-church-state.rationale: Anticlerical; they would abolish both rather than separate them.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Imrie reports Jacob's band robbed priests as 'social parasites' and mocked God at Tours cathedral, while Jacob's trial speech scorned the very laws he was judged by.

private-courts-defense.rationale: They denied any court's right to judge; private ones are not endorsed either.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Rejected the nation and its morality.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Jacob described a war between rich and poor, though illegalists were individualists.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Jacob wanted wealth shared, but the individualists were not egalitarian planners.

civilizational-union.rationale: Hostile to nation and state building.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Hégot sought individual well-being by any means, and critics called them selfish.

restore-past-order.rationale: Revolt against existing order, not nostalgia.

results-over-ideology.rationale: They were practical about outcomes yet fiercely principled about rejecting law; adherents would not give a clear side.

direct-action.rationale: Their whole practice: theft, arson and bombing instead of ballots.

means-match-ends.rationale: Duval defended terror and theft as means, not as prefiguring the future society.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Not an illegalist theme; they lived in cities by burglary and sought comfort, not a return to the land.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The sources discuss wage exploitation but never the division of labor itself.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Jacob said all would belong to everyone, defending theft as the need to satisfy appetites.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Jacob said the more a man works the less he earns and called landlords the worst thieves.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Anti-authoritarian and not tied to the working class as a ruling class.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Illegalists attacked capitalism's injustice but did not theorise imperialism or great-power war.

harm-principle.rationale: Rejected the state's right to judge at all, so they would not grant it a harm-based mandate.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individualists, but not framed in rights language.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Rejected voting but not framed in these terms.

positive-liberty.rationale: Jacob said society offered him only work, begging or theft, tying liberty to material means.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Rejecting the Fatherland and all states, they had no interest in national expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Oaths of personal loyalty to lords are the kind of hierarchy anarchists reject as rule over the individual.

universal-morality.rationale: Jacob rejected conventional morality that treats property as virtue.

workplace-democracy.rationale: They left wage work rather than reform it, so democratic control of firms was not their concern.

economic-freedom.rationale: They wanted freedom from state and property alike but never argued about economic freedom as a condition of political liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: Any government, even one resting on moral example, is still rule over individuals, which they rejected.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Anti-religious, but not committed to rationalism as such.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Jacob condemned wage work as exploitation, and illegalists refused to work.

class-collaboration.rationale: Jacob told the court that those who produce everything have nothing, which can only produce antagonism between the laboring and the owning class, and he 'made war on the rich'.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Reject bourgeois morals and the law.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: State law of this kind is anathema.

state-class-instrument.rationale: They saw state law as class justice favouring the bourgeoisie.

national-mission.rationale: Hégot's rejection of the Fatherland rules out a national mission to export a form of government.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Duval said "the thieves are the rich" and illegalists saw rulers as parasites.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Property protection by the state is just what they attacked.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Debates among state socialists about building socialism were not illegalist concerns.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A state ban grounded in religious morality is the sort of law illegalists said an anarchist ignores.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Strongly anticlerical, they would keep religious teaching away from children, though they opposed state schooling too.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Jacob denied anyone's right to judge him, so authority needs the individual's consent.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: They initiated force by theft, arson and bombings and justified it.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Anarchists were themselves repressed under such laws.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Jacob prized his liberty, independence and dignity as a man.

vanguard-party.rationale: Illegalists did not seek a party leading the masses.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Jacob justified theft from the rich on behalf of the exploited.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing policy never appears in the sources; the question is a state-programme one outside their concerns.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Jacob blamed social structure for poverty.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Illegalists were victims of emergency laws.

party-commands-army.rationale: A party-controlled army is a tool of rule, and they opposed armies and rulers alike.

clerical-rule.rationale: Imrie reports Jacob's band classed priests among the 'social parasites' they robbed and left 'All-powerful god, find your thieves!' at Tours cathedral.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Some illegalists were convicted of offences against public morals and scorned morality.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: They rejected presidents and rulers in the first place, so rules on their tenure were beside the point.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Jacob condemned landlords but individual property is rejected too.

death-penalty.rationale: Duval was sentenced to death and urged comrades to die rather than reach a penal colony.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Anticlerical outlook leaves no room for scripture-based teaching in state schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Convictions for public morals offences; opposed morality law.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship is a state category they rejected, along with the Fatherland and nationality.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Curtailing liberties for state development runs against their demand for personal independence.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Rejected individual property outright rather than conditioning it.

collective-defense.rationale: Military alliances between states are statist and militarist, which anarchists opposed.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Using military force to hold a state together contradicts their anti-state, anti-military stance.

character-from-environment.rationale: Jacob said society left him work, begging or theft.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court policy does not appear in the sources.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims based on nationality rely on the Fatherland, which Hégot and other illegalists rejected.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Political union on ancestry is a nationalist project they would not support.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust is state regulation of the economy, and not something they campaigned for.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: They rejected both courts and majorities.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic blocs of states are statist and nationalist, which they opposed.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding treaty standards are state instruments not in their field of concern.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Illegalists held revolution should be provoked now by acts, not awaited from mass movement.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rule by one society over another is rule they opposed on anarchist principles.

patriotic-education.rationale: Imrie quotes the illegalist press: 'We have had enough of always sacrificing ourselves for something. The Fatherland, Society and Morality have fallen.'

public-money-creation.rationale: A public monetary body is a state institution; they were hostile to the state but did not discuss money creation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Whether capitalism avoids a general collapse is a Marxist debate they did not enter.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Seeking influence over former imperial territory is state power politics they rejected.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory strategy that is not found in illegalist sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Jacob rejected philanthropy as a rich man's virtue; the rich were thieves.

native-born-offices.rationale: Reserving office to natives rests on the nation and on public offices, both of which they rejected.

party-own-road.rationale: An internal question among communist parties that is not an illegalist concern.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Demanding territory back is a nationalist programme in tension with the rejection of the Fatherland.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Jacob stayed anti-fascist to the end; constitutions are not their frame.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: A question about different civilizations' political forms that the illegalists did not address.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A political role for armies is a form of state power they strongly opposed.

office-by-exam.rationale: They rejected holding public office at all, so how posts are filled was beside the point.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: State protection of industries is a statist policy, so they would not endorse it.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: State sponsorship of insurgents is state power politics, which they rejected, though they favoured armed revolt itself.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Armies sent to hold an alliance together are an instrument of state domination they opposed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Jacob called wage work the prostitution of work; state-provided jobs would still be wage labor.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Jacob denied anyone's right to judge him and held that an anarchist need not take the law into account.

informal-organisation.rationale: Gangs like Jacob's Travailleurs de la Nuit were small groups of trusted comrades, and they rejected permanent unions and federations.

national-law-over-international.rationale: They reject all law, national and international alike, so the ranking question has no answer.

religious-nation.rationale: Illegalists rejected religion along with the state and conventional morality.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Illegalists reject the state, law and authority altogether, so ritual submission to any power is rejected.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: They reject property as such and reclaim goods individually; collective ownership of the means of production is not their programme.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Jacob's trial statement denounces the capitalist order as organised theft that exploits workers, not as a stage toward something better.

cooperative-communities.rationale: They put the individual first and reject binding collective structures, though some founded free communities.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Illegalists rejected the state and all its repression, and were themselves hunted as an organised opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: They rejected law, church and conventional morality, so state punishment of religious dissent has no place in their outlook.

alienated-labor.rationale: Jacob called wage work "the prostitution of work" and refused it, which matches the idea that waged labor estranges people from their own activity.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: They were atheists who denied any authority above the individual, whether God, state or law.

property-franchise.rationale: Illegalists rejected the state and its law and held that property was theft, so a franchise tied to property is the opposite of their view.

racial-franchise.rationale: They rejected nation, state and any franchise, and Jacob's band was international in outlook; racial restriction contradicts their anarchist principles.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: They rejected religion and the legal control of private life, so a law restricting marriage by faith is contrary to their views.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Jacob's trial statement and Duval's reclamation theory deny the legitimacy of law and the courts, and illegalists rejected the state outright, so policing and prison have no standing.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Illegalists rejected the state, conventional morality and discipline in service of any nation.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Jacob's trial statement attacks the idle rich who live off the labour of others and defends living by one's own efforts, though by theft.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: They defended violence against the bourgeoisie as legitimate revolt, though Jacob's band tried to avoid killing; they would not renounce lethal force.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: They rejected patriotism and the state, so veneration of the nation's dead is contrary to their outlook.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: They were materialist individualists who rejected conventional morality and religion.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: They rejected the nation and the state, so ethnic ownership of economic life is contrary to their principles.

municipal-property.rationale: Illegalists rejected property in general and took what they needed individually, not for local communities.

family-wage.rationale: Jacob and others rejected wage labour itself and lived by reclaiming what they needed, so a wage standard is not a goal.

person-over-state.rationale: Individualist anarchism puts the individual above state and community; Jacob denied anyone's right to judge him.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Jacob rejected conventional morality and religion; no spiritual programme is recorded.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Illegalists rejected the state and its law and lived by armed burglary and expropriation, so they would never accept a state monopoly on arms.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Illegalists rejected wage labor altogether and saw organised unionism as accommodation, so they opposed bargaining over wages within the system.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Illegalists wanted to destroy the state and its laws, not to capture them; this is central to the current.

sacred-nation.rationale: Jacob and other illegalists rejected nation, state and conventional morality as tools of the bourgeoisie.

workers-own-party.rationale: Illegalists rejected parties, politics and wage labor, favouring individual revolt over any workers' party.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Illegalists rejected legal property and law, so a legal right to own and inherit land is not something they sought.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Illegalists rejected courts and property law, so liability regimes enforced by judges would not be sought.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Illegalists rejected law and punishment as instruments of bourgeois order, so fixed sentences would be abhorrent.

voter-id.rationale: Illegalists rejected the state and elections; identity checks would be state control they evade, though voting rules are never discussed.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Illegalists rejected property as well as the state and law, so a claim of rightful ownership by first use has no standing for them.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Illegalists rejected conventional morality and the established order, which included religious authority, so scriptural authority is rejected.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Illegalists rejected the state outright, so a state is not something to defend whoever runs it.

national-church-status.rationale: Illegalists rejected the state and conventional morality, so legal privilege for a church is opposed.

self-ownership.rationale: Individualist anarchists such as the illegalists claimed the right to live free of wage labour and any imposed duty, as Jacob argued in his trial statement.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: They rejected state programmes of every kind, so neither targeted nor universal provision is favoured.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Illegalists denied that property in any form was rightful, so the rightful-acquisition premise is rejected, and their defence of theft rests on the rich having taken from workers.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Jacob denied anyone's right to judge him, and illegalists held that no law binds the individual.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Jacob described the rich as living off the labour of others, though illegalists drew on this as rhetoric, not a formal value theory.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Illegalists rejected the state, nation and conventional morality and had no attachment to country.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: As individualist anarchists who rejected the state and party, they opposed party rule of any economy.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Never addressed; they scorned state palliatives but not on dependency grounds. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Seeking influence over former imperial territory is state power politics they rejected. (Carried over from former-empire-influence, "A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Theft from the wealthy is justified when it is done to meet one's own needs or to fund a cause.
missingStatements.rationale: Individual reclamation is the defining illegalist practice, defended by Duval and Jacob as taking back what the rich had stolen.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow tactic of one ideology; initiating-force-wrong and taxation-theft already cover property-violation questions.

missingStatements.text: A person has no duty to obey laws that they have not personally agreed to.
missingStatements.rationale: Jacob denied anyone's right to judge him and Antoine wrote that an anarchist need not take the law into account.

notes: Illegalism is a tactic as much as a doctrine; most answers on issues the illegalists never discussed are low-confidence inferences from their anti-state, anti-property individualism. Jacob's gang gave a share to propaganda, while some members refused on individualist grounds.
